# MDL111 · `nul-byte`

<!-- Generated by tools/gendocs from internal/rules: do not edit. -->

A NUL byte makes a line unparsable.

| | |
|---|---|
| Family | loading |
| Default severity | error |
| Fix | — |
| Flags | unsuppressible |
| Design references | K17, cases 56, 67 |

## Why

GLib reads each line as a C string, which ends at the first NUL byte. A NUL before the `=` of a key/value pair, or inside a `[group]` header, hides the rest of the line: GLib sees an incomplete line, rejects the file, and mydumper ignores all of it. NUL bytes usually come from a bad copy/paste or a binary file saved with a .cnf extension.

## Example

❌ Before:

```text
[my\x00dumper]
k=1
```

(`\r`, `\t` and `\xHH` stand for the bytes they name, `·` for a trailing space)

```text
1:4-1:5 error MDL111[nul-byte] NUL byte: GLib stops reading the line here and only sees `[my` (GLib: Key file contains line “[my�dumper]” which is not a key-value pair, group, or comment)
  = mydumper ignores this entire file: it only logs a WARNING ("Failed to load config file") and runs with its defaults, exit code 0.
```

## Configuration

Enabled by default. To change its severity or turn it off:

```yaml
rules:
  severity:
    MDL111: warning   # or error, info, off
```

Its diagnostics mean mydumper ignores the whole file: they cannot be suppressed by comments, only by the configuration or `--ignore`.
